title: Functorial cellular small-object factorization with a smallness cardinal
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal U$. Let $\mathcal C$ have $\mathcal U$-small Hom sets and all $\mathcal U$-small colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and let $I$ be a $\mathcal U$-small set of maps. An $I$-cell map means a transfinite composite, indexed by a $\mathcal U$-small ordinal and continuous at limit stages, of pushouts of $\mathcal U$-small coproducts of maps in $I$. Let $\kappa\in\mathcal U$ be an infinite regular cardinal, meaning that a union of fewer than $\kappa$ sets of size less than $\kappa$ has size less than $\kappa$. Suppose that, for each domain $A$ of a map in $I$, $\operatorname{Hom}(A,-)$ preserves colimits of continuous chains indexed by the initial ordinal of cardinality $\kappa$ whose successor maps are pushouts of small coproducts of maps in $I$. Write $I^{\pitchfork}$ for maps having a diagonal filler in every square with left side in $I$, and ${}^{\pitchfork}(I^{\pitchfork})$ for maps having fillers against all maps in $I^{\pitchfork}$. Every map $f$ has a factorization $f=p_fj_f$, functorial in commutative squares in $f$, with $j_f$ an $I$-cell map in ${}^{\pitchfork}(I^{\pitchfork})$ and $p_f\in I^{\pitchfork}$. Moreover ${}^{\pitchfork}(I^{\pitchfork})$ is exactly the class of retracts, in the arrow category, of $I$-cell maps.
